appraisal_events.evidence: Si Swann était arrivé alors avant même que je l'eusse reprise, cette lettre de la sincérité de laquelle je trouvais qu'il avait été si insensé de ne pas s'être laissé persuader, peut-être aurait-il vu que c'était lui qui avait raison.
appraisal_events.explanation: The retrospective narrator concedes at the outset that Swann's refusal to credit the letter's sincerity was sound judgment, so the scene that follows is framed as evidence vindicating Swann's discernment and impeaching the narrator's own protested purity of feeling.

appraisal_events.evidence: je la tenais serrée entre mes jambes comme un arbuste après lequel j'aurais voulu grimper [...] je répandis, comme quelques gouttes de sueur arrachées par l'effort, mon plaisir auquel je ne pus pas même m'attarder le temps d'en connaître le goût ; aussitôt je pris la lettre. Alors, Gilberte me dit avec bonté : — Vous savez, si vous voulez, nous pouvons lutter encore un peu.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator attains his covert erotic aim and the letter as well, and Gilberte kindly offers to continue, so the dominant local outcome is a realized consummation rather than frustrated pursuit; the narration nonetheless ironizes the attainment by likening the pleasure to drops of sweat and denying him even the time to taste it.

status_effects.explanation: He gains locally: he wins the physical contest, obtains the letter, reaches sexual release, and is invited by Gilberte to continue, though the release is unfelt and immediately shadowed by fear of detection.
His own retrospective admission that Swann was right about the letter discredits the sincerity he had claimed for it, and the concealment he practises on Gilberte confirms the impeachment.
Swann is locally raised as the better judge: the narrator, who had called him insensé for distrusting the letter, now grants that Swann had reason on his side.

ambiguities: The vindication of Swann is stated counterfactually and hedged (Si Swann était arrivé... peut-être aurait-il vu), so it is uncertain whether the narrator fully concedes that his letter was insincere or only that the scene could have been read that way.

Gilberte's awareness is left open (Peut-être avait-elle obscurément senti que mon jeu avait un autre objet), and the mouvement rétractile et contenu de pudeur offensée she shows afterwards would, if she did perceive it, recast the episode as an unwitting violation and locally diminish her rather than leave her standing untouched.
